correctness.rationale: In cumulative pressure x, I'=A−γ/β and J'/β=A(A−γ/β)−IB. Independent rational log enclosures obtained by integrating alternating geometric bounds on 1/(1+u) certify +,−,+,− at the four ordered points of the frozen witness (replay: python /workspace/checks/reproduce.py 1). A decreases and is still above γ/β at the last point, hence prevalence is positive and increasing on the entire witnessed interval and all four points are reached in finite time. Analyticity and the alternating signs give two strict interior maxima separated by a strict minimum. The unique crossing A=γ/β is later and is also reached with positive prevalence; no subsequent maximum is possible. Strict margins give a relatively open set in the admissible parameter space. In a single occupied class the bracket λ(S−I)−γ/β is strictly decreasing while λS>γ/β and negative afterward, so there is at most one strict incidence maximum. If the susceptible mass is zero, incidence is constant zero; the informal strictly-decreasing-or-unimodal description is for positive susceptible mass. The count in the example is a lower bound, not an exhaustive count.

value.rationale: The sharp minimal heterogeneity threshold identifies a genuine limitation of inferring the number or ordering of incidence peaks from unimodal prevalence. Robustness to parameter perturbation rules out a fine-tuned coincidence. The value is as a structural result for a deterministic mathematical model, not as an outbreak prediction or claim about measured epidemic curves.
